name: Thirty-Three Threshold Portraits — Protest Holography
creator: The Threshold Collective (rotating anonymous membership, Tier 1-2 based)
description: A series of unauthorized holographic portrait installations projected onto GLMZ infrastructure — bridge supports, Civic Authority precinct facades, corponation tower lobbies — each depicting one of the thirty-three individuals who died in the 2208 Ochota Sector structural collapse while awaiting Civic Authority inspection responses that had been delayed for eleven months. Each portrait runs for exactly eleven minutes before cycling, and includes the subject's full name, their occupation, and the precise bureaucratic step at which their inspection request stalled. The projectors are hidden and have never been found.
cultural_impact: The Thirty-Three Portraits are credited with sustaining public attention on the Ochota collapse long enough for an independent investigation to be opened — the only time in a decade that a Civic Authority structural failure resulted in documented accountability proceedings.
controversy: Civic Authority classified the projections as 'unauthorized occupation of public infrastructure' and 'emotional harassment of public servants'; two individuals were arrested on related charges but no projector equipment was ever recovered. The families of the thirty-three publicly supported the installations.
story_hooks: A Civic Authority investigator assigned to locate the projectors realizes one of the thirty-three portraits is of her cousin — and she doesn't know whether to file her findings or bury them.
A thirty-fourth portrait appears, depicting someone who is still alive — a mid-level Civic Authority official — and the image is accompanied by documentation of a crime that hasn't happened yet.
The Threshold Collective reaches out to a journalist to offer an interview, but the contact method they use suggests at least one member works inside the Civic Authority itself.
